name: pdk-edgex-device-decommission-purge
instr:
Deleting a device currently leaves its readings behind if core-data misses the system event. Reusing its name can expose the old readings, and buffered events can repopulate them after the delete.

To close this out:
- A successful `DELETE /api/v3/device/name/{name}` in core-metadata atomically commits a durable record containing `deviceName`, `deviceId`, nanosecond `deletedAt`, and `status` (`PENDING` before purge, `COMPLETED` only after core-data has removed that incarnation’s events and readings). `GET /api/v3/device/decommission/name/{name}` returns `{ "records": [...] }`, including earlier incarnations in deletion order. A device without events also completes. Ordinary deletes complete within 10 seconds; after core-data or MQTT recovers, catch-up completes within 30 seconds. Records remain pending while core-data is stopped.
- With core-data `Writable.EventPurge: true`, deleted-device events with origin before deletion are not persisted: HTTP ingestion returns 409 and MQTT ingestion drops them. Data for a new device under the same name, with origin after its creation, survives an old incarnation's purge, including when core-metadata is unreachable and the broker is down. Events for names never registered still persist.
